summary: the flake ledger matches EXACTLY, the deliberate opposite of the stage 2 guard's prefix match

summary: COMMAND NARROWING defeats the flake ledger, and this is stage 3's headline limitation

not_fixed: deliberately - the alternatives were prefix matching, which false-positives across suites, and normalising the command, which guesses. Narrowing is at least a visible act in the transcript

summary: stage 3's CI half is structurally WEAKER than stage 2's and the README must not imply parity

summary: I merged git conflict markers into events.jsonl and main's record stopped parsing
what: three literal lines - '<<<<<<< Updated upstream', '=======' and '>>>>>>> Stashed changes' - were committed, pushed, marked ready, reviewed and merged as 20ea465. The append-only record this whole programme reasons from did not parse for about forty minutes
how: a git stash pop onto a branch lacking the intervening commit conflicted. Git printed 'The stash entry is kept in case you need it again', which IS the conflict signal, and I read the adjacent 'no changes added to commit' as meaning nothing was wrong. A later git add -A swept the conflicted file in
why_nothing_caught_it: four CI jobs ran green on the pull request that merged it. Not one looked at the record. This kit gates commits on a stamp, test edits on a declaration and flaky passes on a trailer - and the file every one of those verdicts is written into had no check at all
found_by: reading full output rather than a filter - the same method that found INC-0018 four hours earlier. A python parse over the file failed, which is the only reason it surfaced
fix: 485927a removes the markers by PARSING every line and rejecting what is not valid JSON, rather than deleting the three visible lines; a bad resolution usually loses events too. 52deea4 adds check-record.sh, 18 controls, 8 mutants killed, wired into the controls job which runs on push to main as well as on pull requests

summary: query.sh --open overstated the open list: it filters per line and never sees a closure
detail: --open selects on '.kind == incident and (.resolved_ts | not)', evaluated one line at a time. It never looks at whether a LATER event supersedes or resolves that incident, so appending a closure does not remove the original from the list
measured: INC-0010 has been superseded by INC-0012 since 2026-09-03 and was still being reported as open three days later. The overstatement was already real before any of today's closures
fix_verified_not_proposed: binding ([.[]|.supersedes//empty]|unique) before the comprehension and excluding matching ids. Tested three ways against the real record: INC-0010 drops with no new events, INC-0016 stays until something supersedes it, and the unmodified record is otherwise unchanged
where: ~/.claude/skills/sre-incident-record/query.sh, outside this repository, so it is not fixed by this branch

summary: stage 3 is INERT: PostToolUse never fires on a failing command, so no failure is ever recorded
measured: probe2, one repo, two sole-command runs against the installed 0.4.0 plugin. python3 test_always_fails.py exit 1 created NOTHING - no .claude directory at all. python3 test_always_passes.py exit 0 created .claude and a four-field stamp. Same repo, same cwd, same command shape
the_script_is_fine: feeding the installed post-bash.sh a synthetic payload with exitCode 1 writes the ledger correctly. The hook is never invoked, so flake_record is never reached
consequence: post-bash cannot observe a failure, the ledger is never written by the real harness, and a re-run pass is indistinguishable from a first pass. That is precisely the hole stage 3 exists to close. The mechanism is merged, public, documented as shipped, and cannot fire
the_contradiction: stage 1's inferred stamp is SAFE because PostToolUse does not fire for a non-zero exit - that premise is stated in this repository's own README. Stage 3 requires the OPPOSITE. Two mechanisms in one kit with mutually exclusive premises, and the conflict was written down before stage 3 was designed
why_the_controls_missed_it: every control feeds a synthetic payload carrying an exitCode, because that is what the design assumed the harness sends. The suites test the script against the payload it was written for, never against the payload the harness actually delivers - which is none
possible_fix_unverified: PreToolUse fires on every Bash call. Recording 'command started' there and 'command completed' in PostToolUse would make a started-but-never-completed test command detectable as a failure. NOT tested, and interrupted calls and session crashes would need handling

summary: flake-triage hooks: fix — observed live and INERT, not merely unobserved
why_not_blocked_any_more: blocked meant 'never observed'. It has now been observed in a live session with the 0.4.0 plugin installed, and it does not work. There is a named defect, INC-0024, so the honest verdict is fix
measured: a real fail-then-pass sequence produced 1788658586|python3 test_flaky.py|inferred|clean and no ledger. The laundered pass earned exactly the stamp this stage exists to prevent
false_positives_note: 0 is meaningless here - a mechanism that cannot fire cannot misfire
the_ci_half_stands: REV-0010 keep is unaffected, though with the hook half inert nothing will ever produce a Flaky: trailer for it to validate - a correct mechanism guarding an empty road
